_comment: Lesson 1: JavaScript fundamentals from the MDN JavaScript Guide - introduction, grammar/types (variables, data types), control flow and error handling (if/switch/try-catch), loops and iteration, functions, working with objects, and indexed collections (arrays). Equivalent depth to the Rust pack's Lesson 1 (7 sections). Sourced from mdn/content on GitHub (main branch), a real, actively maintained public repo - every raw.githubusercontent.com URL and every developer.mozilla.org doc URL below was fetched for real and confirmed 200 before this manifest was finalized (2026-08-31).
_relevanceThresholdRationale: Calibrated 2026-08-31 against this pack's real BM25 score distribution via src/cli/demo.ts (the placeholder 5.0 below was never validated - see git history). An 8-good/8-bad probe found the same class of bug every content pack in this project has hit so far (see README's 'A real, honest limitation'): at 5.0, three queries about topics this pack does NOT actually teach came back grounded on pure vocabulary-overlap coincidence, not real coverage - 'how do I define an es6 class with a constructor and extends' scored 8.14 by matching Working_with_objects' 'Using a constructor function' section (a real but different, pre-ES6 pattern - this pack has no dedicated Classes chapter), 'what is the difference between == and === comparison operators in javascript' scored 8.88 by matching Loops_and_iteration's for...of section (this pack's Grammar_and_types chunks stop at literals and never reach a Comparison-operators section - that content lives on MDN's separate Expressions_and_Operators guide page, not ingested here), and 'how do I query and manipulate the dom with queryselector' scored 5.15 by matching a single incidental 'DOM' mention in the Introduction chapter's JS-vs-client-side-JS aside (no DOM API content is indexed at all). All three are real false positives, not edge cases: an LLM answering from either citation would be explaining something adjacent to, not actually inside, the cited material. Raising the threshold to 9.0 refuses all three (max false-positive score 8.88) while every one of the 8 good probe queries spanning all 7 chapters (variables/declarations 17.87, switch/break 19.73, try/catch/finally 22.00, for/while/do-while loops 21.50, function default parameters 13.33, object-literal properties 10.29, array add/remove 12.25, string/template literals 23.16) still clears it - minimum good score 10.29 leaves a real 1.41-point margin above the worst false positive, wider than either the Rust or firmware packs' own margins at their chosen thresholds. Two other genuinely off-topic controls (cooking, chess) and one clearly-uncovered adjacent topic (promises/async - no Promise/async content indexed) already refused correctly even at the old 5.0 and remain refused. Confirmed residual, found by a follow-up probe and not swept under the rug: 'how does the typeof operator work in javascript' grounds weakly (8.42, via Working_with_objects' Deleting properties section) and would now correctly refuse at 9.0 - typeof is used inside several code examples across the pack but this pack has no dedicated chunk explaining the operator itself, so refusing it here is a true negative (real gap), not a threshold artifact. Same for 'how do I use the fetch api' (5.95, incidental match, already refused well below 9.0). This is the same BM25 corpus-heterogeneity limitation documented in the Rust and firmware packs' own rationales, not something threshold choice alone fully engineers away.
